query.sql:
SELECT
  scope.passages AS passages,
  scope.paragraphs AS paragraphs,
  scope.questions AS questions,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE decision.disposition = 'quarantine') AS quarantined,
  expertReview.answerAgreement.matches AS expertMatches,
  expertReview.answerAgreement.total AS expertTotal,
  expertReview.materialAmbiguityCount AS materialAmbiguities
FROM read_json_auto('output/audits/ielts-reading-rights-matching-headings-2026-08-09/validation.json') AS report,
UNNEST(report.decisions) AS rows(decision)
GROUP BY ALL;

SELECT
  decision.assetId,
  decision.title,
  decision.wordCount,
  decision.paragraphCount,
  decision.headingCandidateCount,
  decision.provenanceStatus,
  decision.rightsBasis,
  decision.factualReviewStatus,
  decision.humanReviewStatus,
  decision.disposition,
  array_to_string(decision.reasonCodes, ' · ') AS blockers
FROM read_json_auto('output/audits/ielts-reading-rights-matching-headings-2026-08-09/validation.json') AS report,
UNNEST(report.decisions) AS rows(decision);

blocks.body: # IELTS Reading Matching Headings — audit gate

## Executive Summary

- **audit PASS; bank and content certification BLOCKED.** The dossier closes F0.2b.5 controls; all 3/3 assets remain quarantined.
- Independent review covered 17/17 heading decisions, matched 17 stored answers and recorded 0 material ambiguities.
- Highest lexical overlap predicts 6/14 eligible decisions; heading ii is correct 0 times.
- The extreme-cue heuristic flags 9 options: 8 are never correct and 1 correct contextual use remains. The learner runtime still offers previously used headings even though the official task contract forbids heading reuse.
- UI/UX and Playwright remain outside this audit-only delta; F0.2b.6 Matching Features is the next unit and was not started.

## The audit passes; the bank does not

The control layer pins 3 passage objects and 17 paragraph-to-heading decisions, applies deny-by-default rights records, and preserves clean-review hashes. Passing those controls is not publication approval. Authorship, license, factual review and independent human approval remain unresolved; answerability conflicts or ambiguities are reported from validation rather than overwritten: none recorded.

## Main idea and heading competition are explicit contracts

Each paragraph must resolve to one Roman-numeral heading through a whole-paragraph main idea, exact supporting language, a paraphrase map and rejection of the closest competing heading. More headings than paragraphs are expected, unused headings are allowed, and one heading may not be used twice. Agreement with a stored key is evidence for auditability, not proof of instructional quality.

## Heading counts reveal a visible gap, not statistical fairness

Across n=17, stored counts are i 3, ii 0, iii 3, iv 2, v 2, vi 1, vii 2, viii 2, ix 2. Heading ii is never correct in this snapshot. The same-position rule succeeds on 5/17; highest lexical overlap succeeds on 6/14 eligible decisions with 3 ties or abstentions. These are content-risk signals, not learner-performance estimates.

## Shortcut and runtime defects block certification

The heuristic flags 9 options containing extreme cues: 8 are never correct, while 1 is a legitimate correct contextual use. The learner runtime still offers previously used headings even though the official task contract forbids heading reuse. With only n=17, the audit explicitly withholds statistical certification; editorial redesign and fresh blind adjudication are required.

## Candidate sources contextualize claims; they do not clear them

The second pass classifies 15 declared factual claims as supported 1, oversimplified 9, unsupported 0, untraceable 5. Candidate institutional sources can support or challenge wording, but they do not establish authorship, licensing, provenance or human factual approval.

## Learning value remains prospective

The clean walkthrough covers 3/3 passages and 17/17 paragraphs. It models whole-paragraph reading, main-idea compression, comparison with a close distractor and repair after lexical matching. It assigns no stored headings or bands and is not evidence from real learners.

## Panel scope

Applicable lanes pass only for a complete, conservative and reproducible dossier. UI/UX and Playwright are not applicable to this unchanged learner-facing delta. Their ➖ marks do not approve the existing interface, accessibility or runtime behavior.

## Recommended next decisions

1. Keep every asset quarantined until authorship, license, factual review and independent human approval are recorded.
2. Redesign the headings and passages, then remeasure, to reduce the 6/14 lexical-overlap signal, the unused ii label and the 8-distractor extreme-cue pattern while preserving legitimate contextual wording.
3. Make the learner runtime enforce the official no-heading-reuse rule, then re-audit UI, accessibility and behavior in a separate learner-facing delta.
4. Re-run clean first-pass IELTS and student reviews after content changes; do not carry forward stored-key agreement as approval.
5. Stop here. F0.2b.6 Matching Features belongs to the next loop iteration.

## Caveats and open questions

The provenance search is directed and non-exhaustive. Source reachability is not verification. Both independent reviews are AI simulations without human signatures. The 17-decision sample cannot certify statistical fairness or instructional efficacy. The report describes the audit snapshot; it does not test the learner-facing interface, accessibility, retention, band improvement or production publication controls.

decisions.title: The changing role of public libraries

audit.scope: Census, hashes, directed provenance search, candidate-source availability and deny-by-default disposition for exactly three Matching Headings assets.
audit.findings: 3/3 assets remain unknown-quarantined. Ten web sources were reachable, but exact-match search was directed and non-exhaustive; visible originality and July-2026 academic-review claims remain observed but unverified, and no rights-holder authorization was located.
audit.blockersCarriedForward: Authorship, license, rights-holder authorization, factual sign-off and independent human approval remain unresolved; PASS is not clearance.

audit.scope: Executable identity, registry contract, two-pass review cardinality, source hashes and denial controls for the audit-only delta.
audit.findings: 3 passages, 17 paragraphs, 27 candidate headings and 17 heading decisions are covered exactly; hashes align and all records fail closed without structural registry errors.
audit.blockersCarriedForward: Bank and content certification remain blocked; the public runtime still does not enforce the official no-heading-reuse rule.

audit.scope: Clean first-pass main-idea adjudication followed by direct candidate-source review; no stored key was shown before decisions were fixed.
audit.findings: 17/17 heading decisions match the stored mappings, with 0 material ambiguities. All three passage assessments are mixed because the tasks are easier and more predictable than a strong live-style IELTS set.
audit.blockersCarriedForward: Agreement is not approval: explicit topic sentences, close lexical echoes, extreme distractors, factual-risk findings and the missing runtime no-reuse enforcement require editorial repair and fresh blind review.

audit.scope: Prospective content-only simulation by an average learner who recognizes lexical-matching and local-detail failure modes.
audit.findings: 3/3 passages and 17/17 paragraphs have a walkthrough covering global reading, main-idea compression, heading comparison, competitor rejection and a repair action without assigning a key.
audit.blockersCarriedForward: This AI walkthrough is not a real-user usability study, retention measure, learning-gain estimate or evidence of IELTS band improvement.

audit.scope: Exhaustive n=17 enumeration of response labels, sequence, position, option length, lexical overlap, extreme cues, set-level reuse, title risk, representation, prior knowledge and packet leakage.
audit.findings: Stored counts are i=3, ii=0, iii=3, iv=2, v=2, vi=1, vii=2, viii=2, ix=2; same-position scores 5/17, lexical overlap scores 6/14 eligible with 3 ties, and nine options trigger the extreme-cue heuristic: eight are never correct and one is a legitimate contextual use.
audit.blockersCarriedForward: contentCertification remains blocked: n=17 is below 100, ii is never correct, lexical overlap is predictive when unique, extreme wording marks eight distractors, and runtime no-reuse is absent.

audit.scope: Not applicable to this audit-only delta: seven learner-facing route/dependency hashes are pinned unchanged.
audit.findings: The dossier records the existing runtime mismatch but does not change or certify DOM, interaction, feedback, responsive layout, accessibility or visual parity.
audit.blockersCarriedForward: This ➖ does not certify the existing learner UI; a separate learner-facing delta must repair no-reuse and receive the full UI/UX/accessibility audit.

audit.scope: Not applicable to the unchanged learner runtime in F0.2b.5; only the portable stakeholder report will receive browser packaging verification.
audit.findings: No learner-facing behavior was changed, and the audit registry is absent from app/component runtime imports.
audit.blockersCarriedForward: No browser matrix was executed for the learner route; report Chromium verification is not learner-facing Playwright evidence.
